Area.evidence_source: ['[page/11/Text/6] Carl\'s previous account highlighted how "L/B/G-friendly" educational environments may not only eliminate the stress associated with sexual orientation-based victimisation, but may even enhance the self-esteem and confidence of L/B/G youth.', '[page/12/Text/2] Preliminary reports of five American Gay-Straight Alliances also demonstrated that such groups may bolster resiliency by providing students with "...aplace at my high school to feel truly safe and included" (Flynn, Lethco, & Page, 1996). Carl\'s account demonstrated that such support during coming-out has the potential to turn alienated suicidal youths into resilient individuals, characterised by renewed confidence and high self-esteem.', '[page/12/Text/3] . . . the support of other gay people is really important, and supportive straight people too, because they are people who aren\'t in the same boat as you, I think it was really important to tell straight people who I was and for them to accept me, I think that was really important because we live in a predominantly straight world. (Sam, 19, non-attempter)', '[page/12/Text/4] Like parents, teachers may be in powerful positions that enable them to play an essential role in boosting resiliency. This is clearly shown in Victor\'s story where his teacher appeared instrumental in providing the support he needed to prevent another attempt:', '[page/12/Text/5] . . . she sees my wrist, and she\'s not stupid, so she just stopped and everyone watched as she cried, she put her arms around me and she took me out of class . . . she just hugged me, she cried and she cried, and I just balled and balled, and she told me she loved me regardless . . . and she saved my life, knowing that someone loved me regardless, and that I was still the person that I was, and that who I slept with had no bearing on me as a human being, or on my life, or all that kind of stuff, she saved my life. Totally, her support was so amazing, she was my tower of strength . . . she carried me through, as did my friends to the best that they knew how, after finding me on the kitchen floor, but you know they weren\'t the most equipped people to deal with a kid on the floor, but my parents would have been if I had them, I so would have drawn so much support from my parents, but I couldn\'t so I draw it from elsewhere so it came from my friends, and It came from my teacher, and the rest of it I had to find within me. (Victor, 18, attempter)', '[page/12/Text/6] Victor\'s testimony impresses how teachers who simply affirm that L/B/G youth are loveable human beings may play a crucial role in resil-', '[page/13/Text/2] iency. Furthermore, it shows that while L/B/G youth may face incredible amounts of heterosexism, it takes just the voice of one respected figure to speak out and tell them that they are worthwhile wonderful people. This highlights the role that supportive straight adults can play to boost resiliency.']
